lots.guide_summary: No evidence survives: nothing sold, unsold or asking. The researcher's web searches were refused (session budget used up) and mine were refused too; LiveAuctioneers and Invaluable keyword pages returned empty script shells. The prior blind $40-90 guess is unverified.

lots.what_it_is: Moroccan koummya-style curved dagger with bone (or horn) grip, white-metal mounts and an engraved white-metal sheath with copper medallions, probably 20th century, tourist or decorative grade
lots.guide_summary: No evidence survives: nothing sold, unsold or asking. All web searches were refused (budget used up) and auction aggregator pages returned empty shells. Value is unverified.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Gowans premium 19.8% would apply.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of type but no hallmarks read and no price evidence of any kind.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Curved single-edged blade with stamped floral marks near the ricasso and some surface wear or staining; pale bone-type grip with applied white-metal floral mount, engraved white-metal ferrule and pommel cap. Sheath is engraved white metal with spiral and scroll work, copper-coloured lozenge and roundel medallions, two side suspension rings and a knob finial. No hallmarks visible; metal looks like nickel silver or base alloy rather than silver.
lots.condition: Appears complete with sheath; light blade wear and patina, grip shows some age colour. Grip material (bone vs horn vs resin) unconfirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Any silver marks on the mounts or sheath? Is the grip bone or horn, and is it cracked or loose? Does the blade sit firmly and is there rust?
